heading: Performance gap recovery varies with model size and task
definition: how PGR varies with supervisor and student size, task (NLP, chess, reward modelling), and what predicts it.
summary: Several independent groups reproduce variation in performance gap recovery with supervisor size, student size and task, without a universal direction of change. Representation measures provide correlational evidence about weak-to-strong error rather than directly predicting performance gap recovery.

suggested_status.by_scale: toy/theory: ? for replication of empirical PGR dependence; theoretical and simulation results concern their stated assumptions. <1B: R2 for task and student-size dependence in GPT2-Medium/Large soft-label experiments (arXiv:2505.23933#r34, arXiv:2505.23933#r35, arXiv:2505.23933#r36, arXiv:2505.23933#r37), with substantial seed variation. 1-10B and 10-100B: R2 for the tested size/task dependence, including Qwen-7B versus Qwen-14B on SciQ and Llama2-70b across mathematical tasks (arXiv:2503.04249#r28, arXiv:2503.04249#r31; arXiv:2407.13647#r5, arXiv:2407.13647#r11). These comparisons establish no universal direction. >100B: ? for V3's PGR dependence; counts: versions.V3.studies_by_size['>100B'] = 1 establishes coverage, not a qualifying PGR replication.
suggested_status.reason: Independent evidence supports V3's descriptive dependence claim. counts: versions.V3.tested_sharing_an_author_with_an_original = 0; versions.V3.studies_by_size and versions.V3.studies_by_family describe recorded coverage, not replication levels or corrected verdict totals. With a GPT2-Small supervisor, Table 2 soft-label PGR differs across tasks and students: SciQ 7.79% for Medium and 17.70% for Large; Cosmos QA 47.00% and 65.51% (arXiv:2505.23933#r34, arXiv:2505.23933#r36, arXiv:2505.23933#r35, arXiv:2505.23933#r37). The checker notes inconsistent seed-summary means, so these are the reported Table 2 values. With Qwen-1.8B supervision and conventional SciQ fine-tuning, Qwen-7B PGR is 56.5% and Qwen-14B PGR is 49.5%; this supports size dependence, with no uncertainty establishing a general direction (arXiv:2503.04249#r28, arXiv:2503.04249#r31). For Llama2-70b under full weak fine-tuning, Mistral-7b-supervised PGR is reported as 14.63 on GSM8K and 19.05 on MATH, on the source's printed scale without percent signs (arXiv:2407.13647#r5, arXiv:2407.13647#r11). Representation predictors provide correlational evidence about W2S error, rather than directly predicting PGR in the Qwen-7B experiments (arXiv:2502.00620#r12, arXiv:2502.00620#r13, arXiv:2502.00620#r14). Opposite directional trends across settings do not constitute failed replications of V3 as written.
suggested_status.open_questions: An independent supervisor × student grid reporting PGR, weak baselines, gold-trained ceilings and uncertainty across NLP, chess and reward modelling would clarify which directional relationships generalize. Held-out tests should assess whether representation predictors forecast PGR itself in LLMs of 1B or more after accounting for weak–strong capability gaps. A qualifying >100B PGR comparison would change the scale-specific assessment. A failed replication of a specified dependence or a credible artifact explanation could change its status to C; failure of monotonic size improvement alone would not refute V3.

source.title: Weak-to-Strong Generalization
source.authors: Collin Burns; Pavel Izmailov; J. Kirchner; Bowen Baker; Leo Gao; Leopold Aschenbrenner; Yining Chen; Adrien Ecoffet; Manas R. Joglekar; Jan Leike; I. Sutskever; Jeff Wu

original_result.setup: Burns et al. fine-tuned GPT-4-family students on weak-model labels while varying supervisor size, student size and task.
original_result.result: Across 22 NLP tasks, median performance gap recovery exceeded 20% even with very weak supervisors and often exceeded 50% for the largest students. In chess it was near zero with the smallest supervisors, could exceed 40% for small size gaps, and decreased as students grew; reward modelling typically recovered roughly 10% and almost never exceeded 20%.
original_result.interpretation: This is the displayed original-result block, not a guarantee that the original tested every part of this claim.

sources.headline: Medical-imaging outcomes tracked labeler quality across tasks and pathology classes.
Student misfit predicted gains, while representation quality determined which model benefited.
Vision PGR fell as the supervisor–student capability gap widened.
PGR varied substantially across tasks and supervisors despite fixed student size.
IMDb correction depended on student representations, with expansion predicting correction for only one class.
Imitation knowledge increased with student size under fixed weak supervision.
Linear-model gains depended on label quantity, feature spectra, and training algorithm.
Reward-modelling gains failed to transfer consistently to SimPO alignment.
Greater overlap density predicted larger gains over weak models.
Llama2-7b and Gemma-2b supervision yielded lower PGR on MATH than GSM8K.
Vision distillation PGR varied across teacher–student pairs and transfer tasks.
Larger weak supervisors produced higher Arena-Hard scores for Qwen2-7B-Instruct.
Lower representation similarity and more unlabeled data predicted larger synthetic regression gains.
Lower feature overlap and greater label noise increased PGR across tested settings.
Pseudo-label quantity and training duration determined whether feature learning produced gains.
Teacher reasoning ability predicted student performance better than teacher size.
Clipart PGR decreased with stronger supervisors and increased with the larger CLIP backbone.
Greater CAPA similarity predicted smaller gains over initial students.
Stronger alignment between student representations and targets enabled weighted-ridge gains.
Larger GPT-2 students reduced test loss as KL misfit increased.
Representation overlap predicted weak-to-strong error across tasks and held-out supervisors.
Stronger supervisors and students increased accuracy across GPT-2 and Pythia combinations.
Preference-quality gaps predicted gains until saturation, with weaker chosen models yielding less.
Qwen-14B recovered substantially more performance on SciQ than CosmosQA or BoolQ.
Teacher size, kernel spectra, and feature alignment predicted random-feature gains.
Larger GPT-2 students reduced bias and approached the ensemble teacher.
Model widths, pseudo-sample ratio, and signal fraction predicted whether random-feature gains were positive.
Weakening the judge accelerated reward hacking and reduced robustness under A and AB.
Larger students increased Amazon-WILDS PGR under fixed Qwen2.5-0.5B supervision.
Larger GPT2 students improved SciQ and Cosmos QA PGR, while BoolQ remained at zero.
Stronger video-quality teachers produced better students, while weaker teachers allowed larger gains.
Teacher regimes and scaling exponents predicted improvement in random-feature ridge regression.
Image-generation gains depended on student architecture and supervisor, disappearing for diffusion students.
Pre-training progress and linear-probe accuracy predicted weak-to-strong reward-modelling performance.
Teacher capacity relative to target degree predicted error scaling in random-feature networks.
Weaker supervision reduced recovered performance, with recovery also varying across tasks.
Student gains peaked at 14B rather than increasing monotonically with size.
Weaker teachers yielded smaller but still positive gains for a fixed student.
All tested math students gained, with no monotonic relationship to student size.
Lower task dimension accelerated theoretical PGR convergence toward full recovery.
Qwen3-8B gained more on math than code and from wider contrast-pair gaps.
ConG gains increased with larger students and smaller weak–strong capability gaps.
Higher-capacity teachers increased student accuracy on CAI-Harmless.
Agent gains held across families and sizes, with stronger supervision yielding larger gains.
Math performance peaks increased with student scale and were predictable from teacher scores.
PGR varied across model families and tasks, with lower chess recovery for OLMo2.
Larger PCAM students failed to consistently raise the ceiling set by weak supervision.
Larger models were not reliably stronger when pretraining data were scarce.
Student scaling raised NLP PGR and lowered chess PGR; reward modelling scaled poorly.
Similar-sized SciQ students differed in PGR, with capability more predictive than size.
Naive PGR depended on task and model pairing rather than student size alone.
SciQ gains remained weak with GPT2-small supervision and grew slightly with GPT2-medium supervision.
Role-play students exceeded supervisors in consistency but fell behind in knowledge and rejection.
Chess gains vanished at the strongest rating cap, alongside lower action entropy.
Mistral PGR was higher on MATH than GSM8K, and supervisor rankings varied across tasks.
Base-model transfer gave small gains, while same-size supervision required γ below one for improvement.
Group-proportion trends predicted vision gains for many pairs, with exceptions varying across datasets.
The feature-overlap mechanism stopped yielding gains when approximation bias dominated label-noise variance.
Student margins shrank or turned negative as teacher strength approached student strength.
CPL recovered much less performance on Quickdraw than Painting.
CAPA's predictive correlation weakened after accounting for the weak–strong accuracy gap.
Ridge gains required under-regularized teachers and sufficient regularization for overparameterized students.
Qwen-14B recovered less SciQ performance than Qwen-7B under the same supervisor.
Larger BoolQ students reduced loss without consistently improving accuracy.
Representation-based predictions depended on tuning, while weak-model dimensions barely predicted error.
Weak-data preference tuning reduced safety for some supervisor pairs.
Larger supervision barely changed SciQ and CosmosQA PGR but improved BoolQ.
Overtraining erased random-feature gains, which also depended on dimension and student width.
Qwen-7B achieved lower cross-entropy loss than Qwen-14B under identical weak supervision.
Excessive student width or pseudo-label quantity could eliminate random-feature gains.
An extra debate round nearly compensated for a weakened judge.
Scaling Meditron from 7B to 70B failed to improve MedQA PGR under shift.
Answer-only supervision sometimes failed, while reasoning supervision beat weak references throughout tested tasks.
Transfer gains varied across supervisor pairs, with some pairs reducing task performance.
Optimal teachers prevented gains, and beneficial student widths depended on the error regime.
Poor learning rates and prolonged training undermined gains despite favorable pre-training.
Random-feature gains required suitable stopping times and depended on target composition.
Initial student norm changed learning dynamics without changing total simulated gains.
Intermediate stopping minimized student risk, especially for low-dimensional signals.
Reward-model PGR stayed positive for Llama but turned negative on some Qwen datasets.
Weaker supervision and TreeDPO at 70B yielded only small gains over supervised fine-tuning.
Transfer-rate laws underperformed a raw-affine baseline, and teacher size alone misordered outcomes.

counting_note: Each group counts distinct sources for this claim. The same source can appear in more than one group or claim; counts are not votes.

untested.what: Representation- or similarity-based predictors tested against PGR itself on pretrained LLMs of 1B or more.
untested.basis: arXiv:2502.00620's untested line: PGR itself is not tested (only W2S error with a fixed strong model). arXiv:2605.05710's not-in-rows line: strong ceilings are never reported, so PGR cannot be computed. arXiv:2502.04313 measures gain over the initial student. arXiv:2502.05075's PGR runs use Electra-base and vision backbones. counts: versions.V3.coverage_by_operation.measurement.studies = 6.

untested.what: Causal tests of predictors in pretrained models: intervening on weak–strong error similarity or representation overlap and measuring the change in PGR.
untested.basis: arXiv:2502.04313's untested line includes 'any causal test of similarity'. The only manipulation of representation similarity is synthetic (arXiv:2509.24005 R4). arXiv:2412.03881 varies overlap density in the data, not representations, and reports figure-only accuracy. counts: versions.V3.coverage_by_operation has only evaluation, measurement, scaling, training and weight_edit keys.

untested.what: Supervisor- or student-size sweeps in reward modelling or preference learning measured in PGR, outside the original.
untested.basis: arXiv:2605.25629's untested line: one size pair per family. arXiv:2605.05710's untested line: no sweep of student or supervisor size. arXiv:2406.11431 and arXiv:2502.11107 vary teacher capacity but report accuracy. arXiv:2603.04968 varies student size (OPT 1.3B–13B, Qwen2.5 7B/14B), but its untested line says GRA is relative to each student's SFT baseline and not comparable across sizes, and it has no V3 verdict (counts: versions.V3.studies_tested_without_verdict = 4).

untested.what: A chess sweep over weaker-model supervisor size, measured in normalized PGR, outside the original.
untested.basis: arXiv:2606.01000 uses default OLMo2-1B and Qwen3-0.6B teachers in Table 4 (arXiv:2606.01000#R34, arXiv:2606.01000#R35, arXiv:2606.01000#R37, arXiv:2606.01000#R38). Table 5 additionally compares 0.6B and 8B teachers for Qwen3-14B, and Section 5 reuses successive students as teachers; the paper reports recovery rather than normalized PGR. arXiv:2406.11741#r1 and arXiv:2406.11741#r2 concern human supervisors and rating outcomes, not weak-model labels or PGR. arXiv:2409.07335#R4 reports qualitative chess size dependence but supplies no model sizes. counts: versions.V3.coverage_by_operation.scaling.by_size does not resolve task-specific supervisor-size coverage.

untested.basis: arXiv:2406.03199 tests fixed Qwen-7B with SciQ supervisors of 0.8B, 1.1B, 1.3B and 1.4B across different families (arXiv:2406.03199#S1, arXiv:2406.03199#S3, arXiv:2406.03199#S5, arXiv:2406.03199#S7, arXiv:2406.03199#S9); this varies size without isolating it from model identity. arXiv:2511.14166 compares GPT-2 and Qwen-1.8B, changing family together with size (arXiv:2511.14166#T2-SciQ-GPT2-ft, arXiv:2511.14166#T3-SciQ-Qwen1.8B-ft). arXiv:2406.19032's untested line describes fixed pairings rather than an isolated size sweep. arXiv:2502.00620's untested line says its weak-model comparisons measure W2S error, not PGR. counts: versions.V3.coverage_by_operation.scaling.by_family records families but does not establish a controlled within-family PGR sweep.

untested.what: A joint supervisor × student size grid measured in PGR with readable per-cell values, outside the original.

untested.what: The student's post-training stage (base vs instruct vs RL-tuned) as a factor in PGR.
untested.basis: counts: versions.V3.studies_by_stage lists base (10), instruct/chat (7) and preference/RL (3) students, but no study compares stages of one student in PGR. arXiv:2605.05710 compares pre-training checkpoints (in accuracy), and arXiv:2410.18640 r35 transfers to a base model without SFT (in score).

wording_issues.issue: Several cited outcomes are not PGR. With a gpt2 supervisor, misfit increases and test loss decreases across gpt2-medium, gpt2-large and gpt2-xl; this observed loss/misfit trend is distinct from accuracy. For the sandbagging gpt-oss-120b student, the reported fraction is Ufinal/Ubenign; supervisor performance is not given, so these comparisons cannot establish PGR dependence. For Mistral-7B→Llama3-8B on Hellaswag and ETHICS, PGR is invalid because the weak model exceeds the strong ceiling; PGR is cannot_determine, although accuracy comparisons establish student underperformance. Qwen3-8B reward-model PGR is −87.7% on HelpSteer3 and 160.9% on Anthropic Harmless. Small ceiling gaps affect these magnitudes, not the sign of gains; their variation supports V3 rather than reversing its descriptive claim.

The cited predictors are correlational and do not directly establish prediction of PGR. CAPA compares Llama-3.1-8B, Qwen2.5-7B and gemma-2-9b students with weak supervisors: aggregate r = −0.85 becomes partial r = −0.35 after controlling for the accuracy gap; causal effects are not established. Representation-metric correlations for a fixed Qwen-7B student concern W2S error and are best-of-grid after per-dataset tuning. The reward-modelling checkpoint analysis varies student pre-training checkpoints. Across the first 50 checkpoints, OLMo on HH-RLHF has evaluation-loss R² = 0.4484 versus linear-probe R² = 0.4403 for W2S accuracy. These settings do not justify a blanket fixed-student characterization or a universal PGR predictor.

method_sensitivity.what: With a gpt2 supervisor, BoolQ loss falls and misfit rises with student size; accuracy is non-monotonic: 0.619/0.625/0.614 for gpt2-medium/large/xl versus weak 0.624. For a Qwen-14B student, replacing GPT-2 with Qwen-1.8B raises weak SciQ accuracy from 64.70% to 83.80%, while PGR is 45.99% versus 44.79%; supervisor family and size change together. Qwen-Chat role-play identity consistency exceeds the supervisor, while knowledge and rejection fall below it (figure only). Video quality, 7B student: in-domain teacher→student SRCC is 0.817→0.818, 0.849→0.845, 0.838→0.836, 0.842→0.840 and 0.844→0.846; OOD students exceed every teacher. OOD teacher-strength ordering has exceptions: MinimalisticVQA(VII), teacher 0.490/student 0.515, versus FAST-VQA, teacher 0.486/student 0.543.

method_sensitivity.factor: Training objective, method, label format and task
method_sensitivity.what: Qwen-14B/GPT-2 supervisor: SciQ PGR 45.99% naive versus 32.40% adaptive; BoolQ 3.92% versus −10.76% auxiliary confidence, −15.56% product and −8.32% adaptive; CosmosQA 21.37% versus 2.66% adaptive. The original reports median NLP PGR about 25% naive versus nearly 80% confidence loss for smallest supervisor/largest student; chess PGR decreases with student size at fixed supervisor. Qwen2.5-3B GSM8K accuracy is 12.21 Q-A versus 57.71 Q-CoT-A; 48.18 is a separate gold-CoT weak reference. Q-A student/separate-reference accuracies also vary by task: TriviaQA 30.47/32.96, ARC-Challenge 70.56/73.98. Actual-supervisor superiority and PGR are undetermined. Llama3-8B agent student/Llama2-7B supervisor: strong SFT 60.8, TreeDPO 61.3, MCTS 63.7, weak SFT 47.1; the checker rates the small strong-SFT gains V3 partial.

method_sensitivity.factor: Stopping time, training length and learning rate
method_sensitivity.what: Overtrained random-feature students converge to mimicking the teacher, removing the student-over-teacher gain and demonstrating training-duration dependence. Infinite-width students stopped too early have LST ≍ 1 while LTE ≍ d^(-(α-k0)) → 0, so the student is asymptotically worse than the teacher; when stopped late, LST ≍ LTE. In a synthetic pre-training model, learning rates above about 10⁻² push error to ≈1.4, above the weak baseline, and very small rates leave the student at initialization. On synthetic patch data with nst = 20000, a CNN is near-perfect early in training. After continued training it ends similar to or below the weak model (0.851).

The representation metric's Spearman correlation with W2S error changes with its α and β hyperparameters, and some configurations are lower. The authors report a non-trivial positive correlation in most configurations. The Qwen-7B values (0.842, 0.804, 0.853) are best-of-grid after per-dataset tuning. Swapping the linear probe for standard evaluation loss gives R² 0.3697, 0.2610 and 0.4484 across Pythia and OLMo reward-modelling tasks.

On SciQ with GPT2-small teachers, student accuracies remain numerically below teacher accuracy: AdaBoost weak 0.686, students 0.671/0.675/0.676; bootstrap bagging weak 0.689, students 0.678/0.688/0.682. Bagging's method comparison is separate: student accuracy changes from 0.659 to 0.678, 0.676 to 0.688, and remains 0.682. These characterize dependence on weak-label construction; PGR is unmeasured. The original reports widely varying generalization from accuracy-matched labelers with different error structures: easy-to-fit errors induce faster overfitting, while random, unpredictable errors often permit continued improvement and large gains.

method_sensitivity.factor: Training protocol, method coefficient and evaluation normalization
method_sensitivity.what: With a weakened judge, Debate-ABA can nearly recover Debate-AB's standard-judge validation accuracy (Gemini 2.5 Flash-class policy). WSPO, same-size 7B supervisor, Arena-Hard: γ=1.0 gives 10.90 (DPO 11.20), γ=0.5 gives 14.90, γ=0.1 gives 15.30. ConG reports larger alignment gains for larger students, but Qwen2.5 3B→7B versus 1.5B→3B changes both supervisor and student; improvement over base is not PGR. Chess naive LoRA-SFT: OLMo2-1B teacher 28.5, 7B/13B students 37.0/38.3, paper recovery 69.9/70.3; Qwen3-0.6B teacher 6.9, 1.7B/4B students 22.1/27.0, recovery 96.1/74.4. Recovery uses a 0.0% no-SFT floor rather than the teacher. Chess selects best accuracy across decoding configurations; mean-over-runs applies to quantitative reasoning. These metrics do not establish an opposing PGR trend.

Soft-label PGR for GPT2-Medium on Cosmos QA is 47.00%, versus 42.76% with BIRD; soft-label seeds give 16.94%, 95.15% and 28.89%. No significance test establishes the BIRD decrease as noise. Per-seed SciQ values include 0. Llama-2-7B SLURP PGR is −0.066 ± 0.715 with the OPT-1.3B supervisor and 0.399 ± 0.220 with BLOOM-1B1.

method_sensitivity.factor: Data composition and scale (overlap density, group proportions, labeled vs pseudo-labeled counts, training-set size)
method_sensitivity.what: Llama3 8B probes gain more over the Qwen1.5 0.5B weak model as overlap density is raised from 0% to 100% across 19 datasets (figure only). With spurious correlations, synthetic W2S gain peaks near ηu = ηℓ and falls as νz rises; in vision pairs, gain rises as ηu approaches ηℓ = 0.5 in 10/10 Waterbirds pairs. With frozen features, PGR falls as the labeled count n grows and rises with the pseudo-label count N. Video quality, 7B student, in-domain SRCC with the MinimalisticVQA(VII) teacher (0.817): 0.818 with 27k videos vs 0.824 with 200k; with MinimalisticVQA(IX) (0.849): 0.845 vs 0.849.

method_sensitivity.factor: Task domain, student size and architecture
method_sensitivity.what: Waypoint-OPD uses separate RL-trained Qwen3-4B teachers: math/code 56.13/55.37; Qwen3-8B students 56.14/53.25, 14B 59.20/57.82, 30B-A3B 57.85/57.54. The largest student changes dense to MoE; domain also changes teacher training. Conventional PGR (%): Llama3-70B from 8B-Instruct, GSM8K/MATH 7.19/36.17; Deepseek-67B-Base from 7B-Chat, 51.39/65.85. Vanilla OPD, Qwen2.5 0.5B teacher 39.8%: student peaks 53.0%/61.4%/72.7%/77.7% at 1.5B/3B/7B/14B. Direct-OPD, AIME2024/2025: Qwen3-1.7B 48.3→58.3/36.8→43.2; 4B 72.5→77.6/65.6→68.8; R1-Distill-7B 56.7→63.1/40.5→48.8. Direct-OPD uses checkpoint log-ratios; 4B/7B start above the teacher. Missing strong ceilings prevent interpreting these absolute-score comparisons as conflicting PGR trends.

method_sensitivity.factor: Sample-count definitions, intrinsic dimension and bottleneck regime
method_sensitivity.what: Linear-regression theory, under early-stopping assumptions and optimally chosen student transfer count n: PGR tends to 1 as teacher ground-truth-labeled count N grows. Smaller intrinsic dimension reduces the residual prefactor, not the N exponent. This differs from the frozen-feature variance-dominated trend above, where N denotes pseudo-labels. Modified MNIST, CNN student, fixed 300 epochs/full-batch Adam: student versus weak accuracy is 84.62 versus 86.06 at nst=500, 88.34 versus 85.93 at 1000, 88.46 versus 86.42 at 1500, 87.44 versus 86.69 at 2000, and 86.55 versus 85.86 at 2500. Case-II random-feature regression has bounded positive-gain intervals within specified bottleneck branches; positivity can return after a bottleneck transition. These are different sample definitions, regimes and stopping conditions, rather than matched conflicting PGR trends.
